Consider the vector field $F=⟨3x-y{z}^{2},\,y+{e}^{z},\,2y\operatorname{sin}⁡x⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by the bounding region of the rectangular solid shown above in the first octant. Given that $S$ is positively (outward) oriented, use the divergence theorem to find the flux of $F$ through $S.$
question.worked_solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(3x-y{z}^{2})+\frac{∂}{∂y}(y+{e}^{z})+\frac{∂}{∂z}(2y\operatorname{sin}⁡x) \\  & =3+1+0 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the rectangular solid enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}4\,\text{d}V \\  & =4{∭}_{R}\,\text{d}V \\  & =4\cdot \text{Volume}(R) \\  & =4\cdot 1\cdot 2\cdot 1 \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$
